commands.review_summary:
The PR adds an `allowBundledFallback` option to outbound channel resolution and disables bootstrap plus bundled fallback at three heartbeat delivery-target resolution call sites while updating related tests to use active-registry plugins.

PR surface: Source +12, Tests -61. Total -49 across 3 files.

Reproducibility: no. high-confidence runtime timing reproduction was run in this read-only review. Source inspection shows the reported path calls `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry` through `allowBootstrap: true`, and current tests prove the bootstrap-backed route behavior the PR removes.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] Maintainer review should decide the heartbeat plugin fallback contract before any automated repair tries to rewrite the activation path.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip plugin bootstrap and bundled fallback during delivery target resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a heartbeat wake-loop latency regression where delivery-target resolution blocks for ~60 seconds per tick when the configured channel plugin is not already in the active runtime registry.

### Background

Commit [`6470bb7625`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6470bb7625) ("fix(heartbeat): bootstrap plugin session targets, #93630") solved a real problem: when a user configured `heartbeat.target` to a channel id that was not in the built-in known-deliverable-channel list (e.g. a third-party plugin id like `discord`), `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel()` returned `undefined` and the target was silently dropped to `"none"`, even when `heartbeat.to` was explicitly set.

The fix was to call `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` in the heartbeat delivery-target path so the plugin could be loaded on demand and the target resolved.

### The regressed behavior

`allowBootstrap: true` does not load a single plugin — it triggers `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry()` → `loadOpenClawPlugins()`, which scans **all** installed plugins. When the channel plugin was not already in the active runtime registry, every heartbeat tick spent ~60s in this bootstrap path before ultimately returning `undefined` (the same result it would have returned instantly).

The heartbeat wake loop was blocked during this scan. The probe measurement confirmed:

```
Before: resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget() → 73,308ms
After:  resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget() → 5.2ms
```

### When this bug is triggered

All three conditions must be true:

1. `heartbeat.target` is not `"none"` or `"last"`  
2. The target channel id is **not** in `listDeliverableMessageChannels()` — meaning the channel plugin is either not installed, not enabled in config, failed to register at startup, or has a typo  
3. `heartbeat.to` is set (non-empty)

Example config that triggers it:

```json
{ "heartbeat": { "target": "discord", "to": "user:xxx" } }
{ "heartbeat": { "target": "my-custom-channel", "to": "someone" } }
```

Config that does **not** trigger:

```json
{ "heartbeat": { "target": "telegram", "to": "12345" } }
{ "heartbeat": { "target": "none" } }
{ "heartbeat": { "target": "discord" } }
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix changes **three** heartbeat-path call sites in `targets.ts` to pass `allowBootstrap: false, allowBundledFallback: false`. A new `allowBundledFallback` parameter is added to `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` (default `true`) so hot paths can also skip the `getBundledChannelPlugin` lazy-load fallback.

**Why this is safe**: Gateway plugin metadata is stable at runtime — installing, enabling, or disabling a plugin requires a gateway restart. If a channel plugin is not already in the active registry when the heartbeat fires, bootstrapping it mid-heartbeat cannot make it usable in the current process. The active registry set at startup is the source of truth for the lifetime of the gateway process.

**Why `allowBundledFallback: false` is also needed**: Even when `allowBootstrap` is `false`, `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` still calls `getChannelPlugin()` which falls through to `getBundledChannelPlugin()` — a lazy-load of a bundled channel module (~14s on first access). The new parameter makes both scan paths opt-out on hot paths.

## User Impact

- Heartbeat wake loop no longer stalls for ~60s per tick when the configured channel is not in the active registry.
- No functional change: the delivery target resolves to the same value as before (`channel: "none"` when the plugin is unavailable), just in <10ms instead of 60s.
- All existing behaviour is preserved when the channel plugin IS registered — the fast registry-lookup path is unchanged.

## Compatibility

- `allowBundledFallback` defaults to `true` — every non-heartbeat caller of `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` is unchanged.
- The `resolveOutboundTarget` (general-purpose outbound delivery) path continues to pass `params.allowBootstrap` through transparently.
- If a channel plugin is already registered at startup, the heartbeat path resolves it from the active registry in the same number of lookups as before.

## Evidence

**Probe measurement** (isolated vitest, `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` with `target: "whatsapp"`, no plugin registered):

```
Before: 73,308ms
After:   5.2ms
```

**Test results** (139/139 passed):

```
src/infra/outbound/targets.test.ts                               85 passed
src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts         54 passed
src/infra/heartbeat-runner.isolated-key-stability.test.ts        11 passed
```

Bootstrap-asserting tests in `targets.test.ts` were updated from mocking `allowBootstrap: true` bootstrap side effects to pre-registering plugins in the active registry and asserting `allowBootstrap: false, allowBundledFallback: false`. This preserves coverage of the same delivery-target behaviors (account validation, target policy, direct-policy blocking) while testing the new hot-path contract.
